html:
On the 1800 map, Rajputs marks the Rajput kingdoms of Rajputana, today's Rajasthan, in a hard time between Maratha raids and British rule. Rajput, from Sanskrit for son of a king, is the name of a group of warrior clans of north India who claim royal descent.

Around 1800 the main states were Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur in Mewar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Kota and Bundi. Many had served the Mughals as nobles and generals. Jaipur's king had laid out a new planned capital in 1727; see Jaipur founded.

With the Mughals gone, Maratha armies of the Maratha Confederacy demanded tribute, and bands of Pindari raiders plundered the countryside. Rajput kings feuded among themselves. In 1817 and 1818 they signed treaties with the East India Company, which promised protection in return for control of their foreign affairs. They stayed princely states in the Rajputana Agency until they joined India in 1949.
